'''''Phoenix loureiroi''''' (commonly known as the '''mountain date palm''', '''vuyavuy palm''', or '''voyavoy palm''',<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Mandle, L. |author2=Ticktin, T. |author3=Nath, S. |author4=Setty, S. |author5=Varghese, A. |year=2013|title=A framework for considering ecological interactions for common non-timber forest product species: a case study of mountain date palm (Phoenix loureiroi Kunth) leaf harvest in South India|journal=Ecological Processes|volume=2|issue=21|url=http://www.ecologicalprocesses.com/content/2/1/21|doi=10.1186/2192-1709-2-21|doi-access=free}}</ref>) is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Arecaceae|palm]] family, indigenous to southern [[Asia]], from the [[Philippines]], [[Taiwan]], [[India]], southern [[Bhutan]], [[Burma]], [[Thailand]], [[Cambodia]], [[Vietnam]], [[Pakistan]], and [[China]].<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 21 January 2018}}</ref> It occurs in deciduous and evergreen forests and in clear terrain from sea level to {{Convert abbreviated|1500|m}} altitude.<ref name=riffle>Riffle, Robert L. and Craft, Paul (2003) ''An Encyclopedia of Cultivated Palms''. Portland: Timber Press. {{ISBN|0-88192-558-6}} / {{ISBN|978-0-88192-558-6}} (pages 402-403)</ref>

''Phoenix loureiroi'' is named after [[João de Loureiro]]; it was originally written by Kunth as "''loureirii''", but this is an [[error]] to be corrected to ''loureiroi'' under the provisions of the [[ICBN]].<ref name=grin/>

==Description==
''Phoenix loureiroi'' contains solitary and clustering plants with trunks from {{Convert abbreviated|1-4|m|ft|sigfig=2}} high and {{Convert abbreviated|25|cm}} in width, usually covered in old leaf bases. The [[leaf|leaves]] vary to some degree but usually reach {{Convert abbreviated|2|m|ft}} in length with leaflets wide at the base and sharply pointed apices. The leaflets emerge from the rachis at varying angles creating a stiff, plumose leaf.

[[File:Phoenix Loureiloi fruits ripening stages.jpg|thumb|Phoenix Loureiloi fruits ripening stages|left]]

The [[fruit]] is a single-seeded [[drupe]], bluish-black when ripe, produced on erect, yellow inflorescences, usually hidden within the leaf crown. The species is noted for its variability in different habitats.<ref name=riffle/>

==Varieties==
There are two [[variety (biology)|varieties]],<ref name=grin/> based on the presence or absence of sclerotic, [[tannin]]-filled cells along the midribs and margins of leaflets:

*'''''Phoenix loureiroi'' var. ''loureiroi'''''.
*'''''Phoenix loureiroi'' var. ''pedunculata''''' <small>(Griff.) Govaerts</small> (syn. ''P. loureiroi'' var. ''humilis'' <small>S.C.Barrow</small>).

==Cultural importance==
Fibers from ''P. loureiroi'' var. ''loureiroi'', known locally as "vuyavuy palm" (also spelled "voyavoy"), are used to make the distinctive ''[[vakul]]'' headgear and ''kanayi'' vests of the [[Ivatan people]] in the [[Batanes Islands]] of the northern [[Philippines]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Phoenix Palm in Itbayat, Batanes |url=http://orerbil.blogspot.com/2011/03/phoenix-palm-in-itbayat-batanes.html |website=Connecting |date=4 March 2011 |accessdate=28 February 2019}}</ref><ref name="Madulid2009">{{cite journal |last1=Madulid |first1=Domingo A. |last2=Agoo |first2=Esperanza Maribel G. |title=Notes on the economic plants of Batanes: ''Citrus'' species and ''Phoenix loureiroi'' var. ''loureiroi'' |journal=Bulletin of National Museum of Ethnology |date=2009 |volume=34 |issue=1 |pages=191–205 |doi=10.15021/00003920 |url=https://minpaku.repo.nii.ac.jp/index.php?action=pages_view_main&active_action=repository_action_common_download&item_id=3928&item_no=1&attribute_id=18&file_no=1&page_id=13&block_id=21}}</ref>
